It solves the parameterization failure of standard NeRF, which assumes the entire scene fits within a bounded volume, leading to either missing background elements or loss of detail due to limited sampling resolution in large-scale scenes [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method solves the parameterization failure of standard NeRF, which assumes the entire scene fits within a bounded volume, leading to missing background elements or loss of detail in large-scale scenes. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in the notes and passages: 'We also address a spatial parameterization issue that arises in challenging scenarios involving 360◦ captures around objects within unbounded environments... NeRF assumes that the entire scene can be packed into a bounded volume, which is problematic for largescale scenes: either we fit a small part of the scene into the volume and sample it in detail, but completely fail to capture background elements; or, we fit the full scene into the volume and lack detail everywhere due to limited sampling resolution.' The source further describes the solution (separately modeling foreground and background using an inverted sphere parameterization for the outer volume) which directly addresses the issues mentioned in the claim.
